extraction_text: Bhima defeated Karna, knocking him down on his chariot seat.
Duryodhana, seeing Karna retreat from battle with his army, ordered his brothers to protect Karna.

attributes.relationship: Duryodhana is Karna's friend and ally

extraction_text: Duryodhana's brothers (including Vrishasena, Durmukha, Karala, Jalasandha, Vikarna, Sama, Dhanurdhara, Virabahu, Alolupa, Saha, and others) charged at Bhima to kill him.
Bhima destroyed fifty chariots along with their warriors that attacked him.

attributes.action: Mass destruction of chariots and warriors

extraction_text: Bhima killed Jalasandha with a crescent-headed arrow, beheading him.
Bhima killed Vikarna and Sama with two more crescent-headed arrows.
Bhima killed Karala with a sharp iron arrow.
Bhima killed Saha and Alolupa while Duryodhana's brothers were in panic.
Duryodhana's brothers, terrified of Bhima who seemed like Yama (the god of death), fled in disarray.

attributes.supernatural_element: Bhima compared to Yama, the god of death

extraction_text: Karna, seeing Duryodhana's brothers being killed, returned to battle and charged at Bhima.

attributes.relationship: Karna returns to fight Bhima after earlier defeat

extraction_text: Karna and Bhima engaged in a fierce and terrifying battle.
Karna, seemingly smiling and with little effort, quickly deprived Bhima of his chariot.

attributes.relationship: Karna gains upper hand against Bhima

extraction_text: Bhima, having lost his chariot, smiled and leaped down from his superior chariot, wielding his iron mace.
Bhima, the subduer of enemies, violently slaughtered seven hundred battle-hardened elephants with tusks like ploughs.
Bhima, knowledgeable about elephants' vital spots, struck their gums, eyes, foreheads, and temples while shouting.
The terrified elephants fled in all directions but were driven back by their riders to surround Bhima, like clouds obscuring the sun.
Bhima, fighting on foot, destroyed seven hundred elephants along with their riders, weapons, and banners using his iron mace, like a great wind scattering autumn clouds.
Bhima then annihilated fifty-two powerful elephants belonging to Shakuni's son in the battle.
Bhima tormented the army, destroyed one hundred chariots, and killed hundreds of foot soldiers in the battle.

attributes.action: Destruction of chariots and foot soldiers

extraction_text: Under the scorching sun and Bhima's assault, the army shrank like a hide thrown into fire.
The army, terrified of Bhima, fled in all directions to avoid him in battle.
Five hundred armored chariot warriors charged Bhima from all sides, shouting and shooting sharp arrows.
Bhima destroyed all these warriors along with their charioteers, chariots, flags, banners, and weapons using his mace, like Vishnu slaying the Asuras.
At Shakuni's command, three thousand excellent cavalrymen armed with spears, swords, and javelins charged Bhima.
Bhima immediately counterattacked, using various footwork techniques to destroy the Yavana cavalrymen.
After completely destroying Shakuni's son's three thousand excellent cavalrymen, the angry Bhima mounted another chariot to attack Karna.
Meanwhile, Karna covered Yudhishthira with showers of arrows in battle and knocked down his charioteer.
Seeing Yudhishthira's chariot fleeing in battle, the great warrior Karna pursued closely, shooting many straight heron-feathered arrows.
Bhima, enraged, covered heaven and earth with arrow showers and enveloped Karna, who was pursuing the king, with a net of arrows.
Karna immediately turned back and covered Bhima with sharp arrows from all directions.
While Karna was attacking Bhima's chariot, Satyaki attacked Karna from behind. Despite the fierce arrow showers, Karna continued to charge toward Bhima.
The two heroic bulls among archers approached each other and exchanged various arrows, appearing resplendent.

attributes.action: Direct confrontation between Bhima and Karna

extraction_text: The arrows released by both filled the sky, forming a massive, terrifying red arrow net like the back of a red-wattled lapwing.
Karna and Bhima fired countless arrows that blocked out the sunlight and sky, making directions indistinguishable.
Shakuni, Shalya, Ashvatthama, Karna, and Kripa engaged in fierce combat with the Pandavas.
The Kaurava army returned to the battlefield and advanced with loud roars like a stormy sea.
The two furious armies clashed at noon in an unprecedented battle.
Warriors called out names and insulted each other's lineage and character flaws.
Sanjaya observed the warriors and feared for their lives, wondering how it would end.
Pandava and Kaurava warriors shot sharp arrows at each other, causing mutual slaughter.
Kshatriyas from both sides fought desperately, wanting to kill each other.
The battlefield was filled with streams of chariots, horses, men, and elephants converging.
Various weapons filled the sky and fell during combat while arrow showers descended like locusts.
Different military units engaged their counterparts: elephants vs elephants, horses vs horses, chariots vs chariots, infantry vs infantry.
Infantry destroyed chariots and elephants, charioteers slaughtered elephants and horses, and charging elephants crushed charioteers, cavalry, and infantry.
Countless warriors fell while calling to each other, turning the battlefield into a slaughterhouse with blood flowing everywhere.

attributes.description: Battlefield compared to slaughterhouse, blood covering ground

extraction_text: The battlefield is described as being covered in blood and body parts, with warriors fighting fiercely.
Elephants attack each other with tusks, and many are wounded or killed by arrows and spears.
Horses are struck by arrows or spears, some collapsing or wandering in pain.
Severed arms and heads fall to the ground, with warriors recognizing relatives or boasting about their lineages.
The battle becomes a chaotic melee with dust and weapons darkening the sky, making it impossible to distinguish friend from foe.
The blood from the battle flows like rivers, carrying body parts and weapons, adding to the population of Yama's kingdom.
The battlefield becomes terrifying with rivers flowing to Yama's abode, headless corpses rising, and demons feasting on flesh and blood.

attributes.action: Battlefield transformation into a realm of death

extraction_text: Famous warriors overcome fear, uphold their warrior vows, and advance fearlessly into battle.
Warriors announce their names, fathers, and family lineages before engaging in combat.
The Kuru army becomes disorganized and struggles like a broken ship in the ocean.
Sanjaya narrates that as Kshatriyas are in distress, the great sound of Gandiva (Arjuna's bow) rings out on the battlefield.
Arjuna (son of Pritha) slaughters the suicide squad, Kosala, and Narayana's army.
The enraged suicide squad showers Arjuna with arrows from all sides.
Arjuna swiftly counters the arrow shower and charges into the enemy chariot forces, reaching the great warrior Shalya.
Shalya showers Arjuna with arrows while the suicide squad also attacks Arjuna.
Shalya shoots nine arrows at Arjuna, three at Krishna's right arm, and a crescent-headed arrow that hits Arjuna's banner.
The great monkey on Arjuna's banner, crafted by Vishvakarma, lets out a roar that terrifies the Kuru army.

supernatural_elements: Divinely crafted banner with roaring monkey

extraction_text: The Kuru army stands frozen in fear upon hearing the roar.
The warriors regain their senses and shower Arjuna with arrows, then surround his great chariot.
They seize Arjuna's horses, wheels, and chariot pole, then let out a lion's roar.
Some warriors grabbed Krishna's massive arms, while others seized Arjuna himself who stood in the chariot.
Krishna shook his arms at the battlefront, throwing all those who grabbed him to the ground like an elephant throwing off riders.
Arjuna, enraged at seeing his chariot seized and Krishna attacked, threw all infantry climbing the chariot to the ground.
Arjuna shot many close-range arrows at nearby warriors and boasted to Krishna about killing thousands of daredevil warriors.

relationships: Arjuna's confidence in his combat prowess

extraction_text: Arjuna blew his divine conch Devadatta, and Krishna blew his Panchajanya conch, their sounds filling heaven and earth.
The daredevil warriors trembled in fear upon hearing the conch sounds.
Arjuna invoked the 'snake' weapon, binding the enemies' feet.
The warriors stood motionless with feet bound by the snake-like weapon, as if turned to diamond.
Arjuna destroyed the immobilized warriors like Indra destroyed demons in battle against Taraka.
The warriors released the chariot and dropped their weapons after being slaughtered.
Shalya, seeing his army bound, invoked the 'Garuda' weapon.

relationships: Shalya as commander responding to threat

extraction_text: Many Garuda birds descended, devouring the snakes, which fled upon seeing the birds.
The daredevil warriors, freed from the snake weapon's bonds, shone brightly like the sun breaking through clouds.
The freed warriors showered Arjuna's chariot with arrows and weapons.
Arjuna, destroyer of enemy heroes, shattered the rain of weapons with his own arrow showers.
Shalya shot a straight arrow that struck Arjuna's heart, followed by three more arrows, causing Arjuna intense pain and making him collapse on his chariot seat.
Arjuna, with white horses and Krishna as charioteer, regained consciousness and invoked the 'Indra' weapon, instantly releasing thousands of arrows.
Thousands of elephants, horses, and chariots were destroyed on all sides by these weapons.
The army was slaughtered and fell into great panic, affecting both daredevil warriors and the king's forces.
Arjuna (胜财) eliminated ten thousand warriors in battle, shining brightly like a smokeless fire.
The remaining suicide squad (敢死队) surrounded Arjuna again, determined to either die or triumph.
Another great battle began between your army and the mighty Pandava Arjuna.
Kripa (慈悯), Drona's son Ashvatthaman (马嘶), Karna (迦尔纳), Uluka (优楼迦), Shakuni (沙恭尼), Duryodhana (难敌) and his brothers rushed to rescue their crumbling army.
Kripa showered arrows like locust swarms, destroying the Srinjayas.
Shikhandin (束发) angrily attacked Kripa, showering him with arrows from all sides.
Kripa blocked the arrows and angrily shot ten arrows at Shikhandin.
Shikhandin shot seven straight-flying heron-feathered arrows that deeply pierced Kripa.
Kripa made Shikhandin lose his horses, chariot and charioteer.
Shikhandin jumped from his disabled chariot and charged at Kripa with sword and shield.
Kripa covered Shikhandin with curved arrows, creating a miraculous sight like stones floating in a river.

attributes.supernatural_element: Miraculous sight compared to floating stones

extraction_text: Dhrishtadyumna (猛光) rushed toward Kripa to help Shikhandin.
Shalya (成铠) blocked Dhrishtadyumna from reaching Kripa's chariot.
Ashvatthaman intercepted Yudhishthira (坚战) and his son/army as they charged toward Kripa's chariot.
Duryodhana restrained the swift warriors Nakula (无种) and Sahadeva (偕天) with arrow showers.
Karna restrained Bhima (怖军) along with the Kalushas, Kekayas, and Srinjayas.
Kripa (son of Sharadvan) shot many sharp arrows at Shikhandin during battle, seemingly wanting to destroy him.
Shikhandin continuously swung his sword, cutting down all the gold-embellished arrows shot from all directions by Kripa.
Gautama (Kripa) shot multiple arrows that broke Shikhandin's hundred-moon shield, causing everyone present to exclaim in surprise.
Shikhandin, now shieldless and completely under Kripa's control, charged at Kripa with his sword like a sick man rushing toward Death's mouth.

attributes.metaphor: Sick man rushing toward Death's mouth

extraction_text: Seeing the mighty Shikhandin troubled and tormented by Kripa's arrow showers, Uttamaujas (son of Yudhamanyu) quickly rushed forward.
Uttamaujas attacked Kripa with countless arrows while charging toward his chariot.
Seeing Uttamaujas engaged with the vow-keeping and formidable Brahmin Kripa, Shikhandin quickly retreated.
Uttamaujas shot nine arrows at Kripa, then seventy more, followed by three additional arrows.
Uttamaujas broke Kripa's bow with arrows and shot an arrow that struck the charioteer's vital spot.
Kripa, enraged, took a new sturdy bow and shot thirty arrows at Uttamaujas, hitting all his vital spots.
Uttamaujas trembled in his excellent chariot, his entire body in pain, like a tree shaking violently in an earthquake.
Kripa shot a horse-hoof arrow that severed Uttamaujas's head, complete with shining earrings, turban, and helmet, from his still-trembling body.
Uttamaujas's head fell to the ground like meat falling from an eagle's claws, followed by his body collapsing.
Uttamaujas's followers, terrified, abandoned fighting Kripa and scattered in all directions.
The mighty Satyaki intercepted Dhrishtadyumna (grandson of Drupada) in battle, joyfully telling him to stand and fight.
A fierce battle ensued between Satyaki (Vrishni warrior) and Dhrishtadyumna, like two eagles fighting over a piece of meat.
In the exchange, the angry Dhrishtadyumna shot nine arrows at Satyaki (son of Hridika), hitting his chest and causing him great torment.
Satyaki, severely struck in battle by Dhrishtadyumna, released showers of arrows that covered Dhrishtadyumna along with his chariot and horses.
Dhrishtadyumna became invisible on the battlefield due to being covered by arrow showers along with his chariot, like the sun becoming invisible during monsoon clouds.
The wounded Dhrishtadyumna used gold-embellished arrows to drive away the incoming arrow showers, shining brilliantly in battle.
Dhrishtadyumna, the army commander, angrily charged at Satyaki, showering him with a terrible rain of weapons.
Satyaki released thousands of sharp arrows to drive away the sudden shower of weapons.
Dushasana's son (Dushasana's grandson) rushed forward to intercept Shikhandin.
Dushasana's son shot a sharp crescent-headed arrow that struck down Shikhandin's charioteer, killing him.
Dhrishtadyumna, having defeated a great enemy warrior, proceeded to shower arrows upon other Kaurava warriors.

attributes.relationship: Commander of Pandava army attacking enemy forces

extraction_text: Kaurava warriors roared like lions and charged at Dhrishtadyumna, renewing the battle.
